sections.text: Transmission Lines
Technical Procedure
Introduction

The purpose of this procedure is to provide 
detailed safe method for transmission lines maintenance staff to minimize the 
possibility of error causing personal injury or damage.
Safety Precautions
A Work Permit must be issued.

Local earthing on both sides of 
work is required.

Wear Your Safety 
Helmet and 
 your Safety 
Belts.

Tools

Material Required 
 Replacement insulators of appropriate size

Work to be Carried

Preparation

Calculate the 
conductor tension to determine the size of rigging required

Obtain a work permit on the 
 circuit.

Attach the handline to the 
 tower arm or leg for convenience in raising the equipment.

Attach the capstan hoist to a 
 leg near the base of the tower to raise and lower the equipment.

Test the conductor for 
 isolation and apply earths in accordance with approved earthing procedures.

Install the suspension platform 
 by placing the hook over the conductor and connecting the chains to the angle 
 steel on the bottom of arm . See Figure 1.

Test porcelain 
insulators to determine the total number of defective units should be replaced 
in the string

Attach a nylon or wire rope 
 sling around the tower tension plate holding the insulators. The sling 
 should be protected from being cut by the steel members 
 Note: 
 A sling may be attached to the 
 tension plate using a shackle if the hole diameter in the plate is large enough. 
 The 
 sling and shackle must have a rating capable of holding the conductor tension

Install a grip on the 
 conductor between the end span terminal and the hook of the suspension 
 platform.

Attach the chain end of the 
 sling and the hoist body to the grip. See Figure 1

sections.text: Replacing Individual units

Lash the insulators 
 to the chain hoist. Leaving the defective units free to be removed.

Take up on the hoist to allow 
 enough slack in the insulator string to disconnect the defective units

Replace the defective units 
 and remove the lashing ropes.

Release the tension on the 
 hoist checking that all the sockets and keys are properly positioned.

Remove the equipment and lower 
 it to the ground.

Replacing The Complete Insulator 
String

-Install a second grip on the 
 conductor and connect a snatch block to the grip. See figure 2.

-Attach a second snatch block 
 to the arm near the tension plate using a sling.

-Tie a 19 mm (3/4 in ) rope to 
 the third insulator from the lin or outer end and insert the rope through the 
 two snatch blocks as shown in figure 2.

-Lash the conductor end span 
 terminal to the chain hoist to avoid bending the conductor near the 
 grip.

-Take up on the chain hoist to 
 slacken the insulator string.

-Attach the rope to the capstan 
 hoist and then take up on the rope to hold the line end of the insulator 
 string.

-Disconnect the line end 
 insulator from the conductor end span terminal.

-Slacken the rope allowing the 
 insulator string to swing below the tower plate.

-Remove the rope from the 
 snatch block that is attached to the conductor grip.

- Install the insulator lifting 
 yoke under the third insulator from the tower end.

-Tie the rope to the insulator 
 lifting yoke when enough slack is obtained in the rope as shown in figure 3 
 .

-Take up on the rope to allow 
 the insulator string to be disconnected from the plate.

-Disconnect the insulator 
 string from the capstan Hoist - Reverse this procedure.

-Reverse this procedure to 
 return the insulator string to its normal position.

Safety Summary

The following hazards and 
precautions are emphasized to highlight some of the safety considerations
related to this job.

Other hazards, which are site specific and
of a general nature must be identified during the 
tailboard conference before the work commences.

Hazard 
Precaution

Electrical 
 - Obtain a work permit on the circuit.

- Test for isolation and apply temporary earths
using approved earthing procedures.

Mechanical 
- Calculate the conductor tension to check the
loading on the rigging.
- Check that all the insulator sockets and keys are properly positioned .

Work 
Aloft 
- Use approved fall protection.

Communication 
- Good verbal communication is required of all crew members.
